subject: psychiatry
title: Narcissistic, Cluster C Anxious Personalities, and Dialectical Behaviour Therapy

steps.tx: **Narcissistic personality disorder** is characterized by a pervasive pattern of grandiosity in fantasy or behavior, a constant need for excessive admiration, and a profound lack of empathy. Sufferers harbor an exaggerated sense of self-importance, demand special treatment, exploit interpersonal relationships, and react with rage to minor critiques.
steps.say: Narcissistic personality disorder involves grandiosity, entitlement, a need for admiration, and a lack of empathy, masking fragile self-esteem.

vis.title: Narcissistic Diagnostic Criteria
rows: Expects to be recognized as superior without merit
Takes advantage of others to achieve ends
Views friends and colleagues as functional tools
Unwilling to recognize feelings of others
Callous emotional dismissal of family needs

steps.tx: Two patients may both sit alone at a party for opposite reasons. One scans the room wishing someone would talk, yet stays silent because a clumsy word might earn ridicule. The other feels no pull toward company at all and leaves early without regret. Longing held back by fear marks **avoidant personality disorder**, whereas genuine indifference to company marks its schizoid counterpart.
steps.say: Avoidant patients want friends but fear rejection, while schizoid patients are simply indifferent to relationships.

vis.alt: Two contrasting figures, one wanting to join a group but holding back from fear of rejection and one indifferent to company
vis.caption: A person longing to join others but held back by fear of rejection, contrasted with one who feels no interest in company. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Cluster C personality disorders** encompass avoidant, dependent, and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders, unified by pervasive anxious, fearful, or perfectionistic behaviors. These conditions demonstrate strong epidemiological and genetic associations with anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, and high behavioral inhibition that restrict spontaneous interpersonal engagement.
steps.say: Cluster C includes avoidant, dependent, and obsessive-compulsive personalities, unified by pervasive anxious and fearful traits.

vis.title: Cluster C Anxious Spectrum
rows: Fear of rejection, humiliation, and criticism
Total social withdrawal despite desiring friends
Extreme submissiveness and urgent relationship seeking
Fear of error, disorder, and loss of control

steps.tx: **Avoidant personality disorder** features a pervasive pattern of social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy, and hypersensitivity to negative evaluation. Sufferers avoid occupational activities involving significant interpersonal contact due to fears of criticism, disapproval, or rejection, viewing themselves as socially inept, unappealing, or inferior to others.
steps.say: Avoidant individuals avoid social contact due to terror of embarrassment and rejection, despite desperately yearning for close relationships.

left.title: Avoidant Personality
points: Desperately desires warm friendships
Avoids intimacy due to fear of humiliation
Views self as socially inept and inferior
Pervasive across all life domains

right.title: Social Anxiety Disorder
points: Fear circumscribed to public performance
Insight into irrationality of anxiety
More responsive to acute SSRI therapy
Episodic exacerbations with public tasks

steps.tx: **Dependent personality disorder** is characterized by a pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of, leading to submissive, clinging behavior and fears of separation. Sufferers struggle to make everyday decisions without extensive advice and reassurance, delegate responsibility for major areas of life, and urgently seek replacements when relationships end.
steps.say: Dependent personality involves an excessive need to be cared for, leading to clinging submissiveness, indecision, and terror of being alone.

vis.title: Dependent Behavioral Phenotype
rows: Cannot choose clothing or meals without advice
Total loss of personal autonomy and agency
Agrees with abusive partners to avoid abandonment
Demands spouse manage finances, jobs, housing
Severe panic upon partner illness or separation

steps.tx: **Anankastic obsessive-compulsive personality disorder** is defined by a pervasive preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism, and mental and interpersonal control, at the expense of flexibility, openness, and efficiency. Hallmarks include excessive devotion to work excluding leisure, extreme moral scrupulosity, reluctance to delegate tasks, and stubborn stinginess.
steps.say: Obsessive-compulsive personality involves rigid perfectionism and orderliness that paralyzes efficiency, viewed by the patient as correct.

left.title: OCPD (Ego-Syntonic)
points: Perfectionism viewed as purposeful and correct
Absence of true obsessions or cleaning rituals
Preoccupation with rules, lists, and schedules
Interpersonal stubbornness and micromanagement

right.title: OCD (Ego-Dystonic)
points: Intrusive thoughts recognized as senseless
Accompanied by time-consuming compulsions
High internal distress and suffering
Responds to high-dose SSRIs and ERP

steps.tx: **Splitting defense mechanism** is a primitive psychological defense classically operational in borderline personality disorder, characterized by failure to integrate positive and negative qualities of the self or others into cohesive images. The individual categorizes people into mutually exclusive extremes: completely all-good or completely all-bad.
steps.say: Splitting is a primitive defense in borderline personality that divides people into all-good or all-bad, rapidly alternating between idealization and hatred.

left.title: All-Good Idealization
points: Individual viewed as perfect and omnipotent
Intense affection and complete emotional devotion
Blind to real human shortcomings or boundaries
Vulnerable to catastrophic disappointment

right.title: All-Bad Devaluation
points: Triggered by minor delay or perceived slight
Target instantly viewed as evil and cruel
Intense verbal hostility, rage, and hatred
Complete amnesia for previous loving feelings

steps.tx: Therapy for the instability just described is taught as four practical skill sets rather than insight alone. The picture lays out **dialectical behaviour therapy** as mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation and interpersonal effectiveness, each practised between sessions. Patients rehearse these modules in group skills training while individual therapy and phone coaching help them use the same steps during real crises at home or work.
steps.say: Dialectical behaviour therapy teaches four skill modules: mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation and interpersonal effectiveness. Group practice plus coaching transfers those skills into daily crises.

vis.alt: Four labelled DBT skill modules arranged around a patient: mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation and interpersonal effectiveness
vis.caption: Four DBT skill modules surround the patient: mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion regulation and interpersonal effectiveness. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Dialectical behaviour therapy**, formulated by Marsha Linehan, represents the gold standard evidence-based psychotherapy specifically engineered for borderline personality disorder. DBT balances the philosophical dialectic between radical acceptance and validation of emotional suffering on one hand, with systematic training in behavioral change on the other.
steps.say: Dialectical behaviour therapy balances radical acceptance with behavioral change, providing the gold standard treatment for borderline personality.

nodes.label: Core mindfulness: non-judgmental present moment awareness
Distress tolerance: crisis survival skills without self-harm
Emotion regulation: identifying and modifying intense emotional waves
Interpersonal effectiveness: assertiveness and boundary maintenance

steps.tx: **Ego-syntonic versus ego-dystonic distinction** fundamental to psychiatric nosology differentiates personality disorders from axis I clinical syndromes. In ego-syntonic conditions, such as narcissistic personality, symptoms and behaviors are perceived as natural, acceptable, and consistent with the authentic self; in ego-dystonic conditions, symptoms cause acute distress.
steps.say: Ego-syntonic traits feel natural and integral to the patient, whereas ego-dystonic symptoms feel foreign, distressing, and alien.

left.title: Ego-Syntonic Traits
points: Seen in personality disorders and mania
Behaviors felt as natural and integral to self
Patient rationalizes and defends traits
Seeks treatment only when pressured by others

right.title: Ego-Dystonic Symptoms
points: Seen in OCD, depression, and panic disorder
Symptoms experienced as foreign and unwanted
Causes acute personal suffering and anguish
Patient actively seeks medical help for relief
